Two-dimensional UMAP of every stimulus image in every format, from the embeddings written by
`pipeline/12_embeddings.py` (DINOv3 ViT-B/16 and CLIP ViT-B/32; cosine metric). Illustration history rounds are
left out.

```{python}
#| include: false
import sys, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore'); sys.path.insert(0, '../pipeline')
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, umap
from config import OUT, pairs, words
P, W = pairs(), words()
ORDER = ['CHS photo', 'photo', 'cutout', 'illustration', 'illustration_cutout', 'line', 'line_cutout', 'doodle', 'doodle_cutout']
MODELS = {'dinov3': 'DINOv3 ViT-B/16', 'clip': 'CLIP ViT-B/32'}
pair_of = {w: r.pair for r in P.itertuples() for w in (r.word_a, r.word_b)}
FC = dict(zip(ORDER, plt.cm.tab10.colors))
PC = {p: plt.cm.tab20(i % 20) for i, p in enumerate(P.pair)}
MK = dict(zip(ORDER, 'XosD^vP<>'))

def load(model):
    z = np.load(f'{OUT}/embeddings_{model}.npz'); k = pd.DataFrame([s.split('|') for s in z['key']], columns=['version', 'word'])
    keep = k.version.isin(ORDER).values
    return k[keep].reset_index(drop=True), z['emb'][keep]

def run(X, seed=0):
    return umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=.3, metric='cosine', random_state=seed).fit_transform(X)
data = {m: load(m) for m in MODELS}
```

## All formats together

Coloured by format (left) and by pair (right, marker = format). Lines join the two images of a pair within a format.

```{python}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 12
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
for row, (m, name) in zip(axes, MODELS.items()):
    k, X = data[m]; U = run(X); k = k.assign(x=U[:, 0], y=U[:, 1])
    fm = [f for f in ORDER if f in set(k.version)]
    for f in fm:
        s = k[k.version == f]; row[0].scatter(s.x.values, s.y.values, s=22, color=FC[f], label=f)
    row[0].set_title(f'{name}: by format'); row[0].legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False, markerscale=1.3)
    for r in P.itertuples():
        for f in fm:
            s = k[(k.version == f) & k.word.isin([r.word_a, r.word_b])]
            if len(s) == 2: row[1].plot(s.x.values, s.y.values, color=PC[r.pair], lw=.7, alpha=.6)
    for f in fm:
        s = k[k.version == f]; row[1].scatter(s.x.values, s.y.values, s=26, c=[PC[pair_of[w]] for w in s.word], marker=MK[f], label=f)
    for r in P.itertuples():
        s = k[k.word.isin([r.word_a, r.word_b])]; row[1].text(s.x.mean(), s.y.mean(), r.pair, fontsize=6.5, color=PC[r.pair])
    row[1].set_title(f'{name}: by pair (marker = format)'); row[1].legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False)
    for ax in row: ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
fig.tight_layout()
```

Format dominates: each format forms its own cloud, which is the shared-style baseline from
`02_format_similarity`. Item structure is visible only within a cloud.

## With the shared style removed

Subtract each format's mean embedding (and re-normalise) before UMAP. What remains is how each image differs from
the rest of its format, so items can line up across formats if the model sees the same object in them.

```{python}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 6
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))
for ax, (m, name) in zip(axes, MODELS.items()):
    k, X = data[m]; Xc = X.copy()
    for f in k.version.unique():
        i = (k.version == f).values; Xc[i] -= Xc[i].mean(0)
    Xc /= np.linalg.norm(Xc, axis=1, keepdims=True); U = run(Xc); k = k.assign(x=U[:, 0], y=U[:, 1])
    fm = [f for f in ORDER if f in set(k.version)]
    for f in fm:
        s = k[k.version == f]; ax.scatter(s.x.values, s.y.values, s=26, c=[PC[pair_of[w]] for w in s.word], marker=MK[f], label=f)
    for r in P.itertuples():
        s = k[k.word.isin([r.word_a, r.word_b])]; ax.text(s.x.mean(), s.y.mean(), r.pair, fontsize=7, color=PC[r.pair])
    ax.set_title(f'{name}, format means removed: by pair (marker = format)'); ax.legend(fontsize=8, frameon=False)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
fig.tight_layout()
```

How well does each format's version of a word find the same word in the other formats? For each image, the share of
the other formats in which its nearest neighbour (cosine, format means removed) is the same word:

```{python}
for m, name in MODELS.items():
    k, X = data[m]; Xc = X.copy()
    for f in k.version.unique():
        i = (k.version == f).values; Xc[i] -= Xc[i].mean(0)
    Xc /= np.linalg.norm(Xc, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    fm = [f for f in ORDER if f in set(k.version)]; M = pd.DataFrame(index=fm, columns=fm, dtype=float)
    for f in fm:
        for g in fm:
            if f == g: continue
            a, b = k[k.version == f], k[k.version == g]
            S = Xc[a.index] @ Xc[b.index].T
            M.loc[f, g] = np.mean(b.word.values[S.argmax(1)] == a.word.values)
    print(name, '(row = query format, column = searched format; chance ≈ 1/32)'); print(M.round(2).to_string(), '\n')
```

The illustrations are traced from the same photos (same crop, same layout), so matching between photo, cut-out and
illustration versions is expected to be near perfect. Only the CHS-photo rows and columns, which use different
exemplars, measure whether the model finds the *same word* rather than the same picture.
